summary: The note describes Vulcan Productions, a Seattle television and film production company run by Paul Allen and his sister Jody Allen as owners and executive producers. It is part of the entertainment division of Vulcan Inc. The note says the company's films have won many awards and nominations, including a 2014 Webby, and lists its films and documentary projects from 2002 to 2015.
one_line: Overview of Vulcan Productions, the Seattle film and television company run by Paul and Jody Allen, its awards, and its projects from 2002 to 2015.
key_facts: Paul Allen and his sister Jody Allen together were the owners and executive producers of Vulcan Productions.
Vulcan Productions is a television and film production company headquartered in Seattle.
Vulcan Productions operates within the entertainment division of Vulcan Inc.
The films of Vulcan Productions have received recognition ranging from a Peabody to Independent Spirit Awards, Grammys and Emmys.
In 2014, the Vulcan Productions film "We The Economy" won 12 awards, including a Webby award for best Online News & Politics Series.
The films of Vulcan Productions have also been nominated for Golden Globes and Academy Awards, among many others.
Vulcan Productions' films and documentary projects include "Far from Heaven" (2002).
Vulcan Productions' films and documentary projects include "Hard Candy" (2005).
Vulcan Productions' films and documentary projects include "Rx for Survival: A Global Health Challenge" (2005).
Vulcan Productions' films and documentary projects include "Where God Left His Shoes" (2006).
Vulcan Productions' films and documentary projects include "This Emotional Life" (2010).
Vulcan Productions' films and documentary projects include "We The Economy" (2014).
Vulcan Productions' films and documentary projects include "Racing Extinction" (2015).
Vulcan Productions' films and documentary projects include the Oscar-nominated "Body Team 12" (2015).
